props.title: Son of the White Mare
props.initialSlug: Ancient Hungarian myths explode in psychedelic glory

sections.content: Son of the White Mare (1981) stands as Hungarian animator Marcell Jankovics's psychedelic masterpiece, transforming ancient Magyar folklore into a kaleidoscopic explosion of color and motion. The film's pulsating, shape-shifting animation style revolutionized what was possible in hand-drawn animation, predating similar visual experiments in Mind Game (2004) and Redline (2009). Its influence extends to modern works like The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013), particularly in how it uses morphing character designs to express emotional states.

sections.content: The film's treatment of Hungarian mythology parallels other ambitious animated adaptations of cultural folklore. The Secret of Kells (2009) does similar work with Celtic mythology, while The Legend of Hei (2019) draws from Chinese folklore. What sets Son of the White Mare apart is its complete commitment to abstract visualization - characters transform into geometric patterns, backgrounds pulse with primary colors, and traditional narrative structure dissolves into dream-logic sequences.

Jankovics's technical innovations in animation deserve special focus. The film pioneered techniques for fluid character transformation that wouldn't become common until digital animation in films like Paprika (2006). Its bold use of limited color palettes influenced later experimental animators like Don Hertzfeldt, particularly in It's Such a Beautiful Day (2012). The film's marriage of traditional folklore with avant-garde visuals created a template for modern animated features like Wolf Children (2012). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Animation

sections.content: Contemporary animation continues to draw from Son of the White Mare's fearless experimentation. Love, Death & Robots (2019) episodes frequently echo its morphing animation style. The fluid transformations in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018) owe a debt to Jankovics's pioneering work. Even traditionally animated films like The Night Is Short, Walk On Girl (2017) show traces of its influence in their more experimental sequences.
